title: Verifier‑Grounded, Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study (estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that evaluated the preregistered estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under the frozen generation semantics shared_initial_candidate. Using N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), the deterministic template baseline passed the verifier on 120/120 tasks and the single canonical LLM candidate (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini) also passed 120/120 tasks (paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). We publish the complete execution and scoring artifacts (see execution/execution_manifest.json) and show—using the archived canonical candidates (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...) and per‑episode validator traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...)—why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics deterministically collapses the paired contrast. We then provide artifact‑grounded, runnable experimental modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory designs, validator diversification, expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question of independent generative reliability.

sections.introduction: Translating high‑level operator intent into device configuration is an operationally critical NetOps task where semantic correctness (reachability, ACL/routing preservation, transient safety during multi‑step changes) is required before deployment. Deterministic offline validators provide auditable safety oracles for candidate configurations; coupling LLM generation to such verifiers yields generate→validate→repair pipelines that can be operationally meaningful. We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) a confirmatory paired test whose exact estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated under the preregistered generation semantics shared_initial_candidate (i.e., one canonical LLM candidate generated per task and reused for both scoring conditions). Our goals: (1) publish a fully reproducible artifact bundle; (2) execute the preregistered confirmatory analysis and report exact, archived counts and inferential results; (3) diagnose, using the same artifacts, why the confirmatory pairing produced a degenerate contingency; and (4) propose immediate, artifact‑grounded reruns that answer the operational question practitioners typically need (independent per‑condition generative reliability).
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps: Deterministic configuration analyzers (Batfish and successors) are established tools for control‑plane and data‑plane verification and are operationally used for predeployment checks [Brown et al., 2023; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent LLM→NetOps research explores intent→config generation, often within generate→validate→repair workflows and varying on three key axes: sampling semantics (single canonical vs independent draws), repair budget (single pass vs bounded iterations), and validator scope (syntax vs reachability+ACL+routing checks). Independent sampling plus multi‑seed replication is required to estimate an LLM’s operational generative reliability; shared‑candidate designs instead measure validator behavior under identical inputs. We position our study as a preregistered, artifact‑anchored demonstration of the latter estimand and provide contrasts to independent‑sampling evaluations (see evidence bundle).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and artifacts. The study preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1) was frozen prior to any model calls (SHA‑256 7db1663c...). The declared model and adapter: gpt‑5‑mini via adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model config archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The immutable initial master prompt is preserved at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Task bank and templates. We synthesized N = 120 tasks (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS) using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (generator_version 5.0). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit required_sequence, per‑task workflow_policies (must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), and difficulty metadata. Representative manifests and hashes are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl (full manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). Generation and confirmatory semantics. The preregistered, frozen confirmatory generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate": for each task we generated one canonical LLM candidate (shared_initial) and reused that identical candidate for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes; shared candidate files are archived (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt; exemplar SHA‑256s: task-000001 8f38c8be..., task‑000002 ae967f70..., task‑000003 f7f4db24...). Validator and scoring. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). The scoring rule for the primary estimand was full_intent_constraint_validation (binary pass only if all required commands and transient constraints are satisfied). Each scored episode produced a detailed JSON trace archived at execution/scoring/*.json (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...). Analysis plan. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline over N = 120 pairs. Primary inferential procedure: paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test on the 2×2 paired table. Missingness/retry policy: up to 2 automated retries for infrastructure failures; preregistered treatment of failed calls documented; none triggered. All provider calls, call cache, seeds and per‑episode artifacts are archived for byte‑for‑byte reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json contains exhaustive SHA‑256 map).

Baseline verifier passes = 120/120; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini canonical shared_initial) verifier passes = 120/120. Paired contingency table: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Paired estimate = 0.00. Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative scoring traces: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...) shows parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4 and validation_after.valid = true; canonical candidate used: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...). Contamination heuristics (preregistered string‑overlap thresholds) recorded no flags in analysis/contamination_summary.csv, but the preregistered statement warns that overlap heuristics are imperfect proxies for pretraining exposure.
sections.discussion:
Why the confirmatory contingency is degenerate (artifact evidence). The archival chain shows two preregistered, artifact‑visible design choices that deterministically produce the observed collapse: (1) generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (a single canonical LLM output per task archived under execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt and reused across both scoring episodes) and (2) template‑tight tasks with explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies which canonical template‑aligned outputs satisfy. A deterministic validator applied to identical inputs necessarily returns identical pass/fail outputs, producing n_11 = 120. This causal chain is fully reconstructable from the published artifacts (execution/responses/..., execution/scoring/..., execution/execution_manifest.json) and therefore the confirmatory result is correct for the preregistered estimand but not informative about independent per‑condition generative reliability.

What the confirmatory result does and does not imply. It correctly answers whether the deterministic validator treats identical candidates differently across two scoring conditions (it does not). It does not answer the operational question practitioners usually require: the probability that independently drawn LLM candidates will satisfy verifier constraints when sampled under deployment‑like stochasticity. Estimating that quantity requires independent_per_condition sampling or multi‑seed replication per condition.

Runnable, artifact‑grounded remediation (preserving reproducibility). Using the published bundle one can deterministically run immediately informative reruns: (A) independent_per_condition rerun: generate distinct seeds per condition per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1), rescore with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and recompute the paired estimator; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design: draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification: add a second independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates. All required components (task generator, provider call traces, response I/O, validator harness) are archived with SHA‑256 fingerprints in execution/execution_manifest.json to ensure deterministic reruns. These reruns convert a degenerate paired design into an informative operational comparison while remaining fully reproducible.
sections.conclusion: We executed the preregistered confirmatory study and published the exhaustive artifact bundle needed for byte‑for‑byte reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json and per‑file SHA‑256s). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both baseline and gpt‑5‑mini canonical candidates passed the deterministic validator on all N = 120 tasks (120/120 each). The archived artifacts show that identical canonical candidates plus a deterministic validator produced the degenerate paired contingency; consequently the confirmatory paired result answers the preregistered estimand correctly but does not estimate independent generative reliability. We provide immediate, artifact‑grounded rerun options (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed designs, validator diversification) that preserve reproducibility while producing operationally informative estimates. All artifacts referenced here (model configuration, shared candidates, scoring traces, and the preregistration and master prompt immutable references) are included in the submission bundle to enable deterministic auditing and follow‑up experiments.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
